title: Handoff: tensor-core kernels for the dense (non-expert) matmuls of Shadow's prompt path
written: 2026-11-02, mid-task; the previous AI may have run out of tokens. Read docs/STATUS.md (last 4 entries dated 2026-11-02) first.
repo: J:\Shadow (git, branch main, remote https://github.com/a3k6g3d/Shadow-Engine). Commit trailer: 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>'. Windows; use Bash tool with forward slashes or PowerShell. CRLF files: edit with small Python scripts (open(newline='') and convert) or single-line Edit anchors.
goal: Raise prompt-reading speed (tokens/s of a long prompt) from ~192-212 tok/s toward Strata's 1,376 by replacing the slow dense `matvec_cols_*` kernels (<=8 tokens per launch, so a 2,048-token pass re-reads every weight row ~256 times) with tensor-core `mma_cols_*` kernels under --tensor-prompt.
why_this_and_not_cpu_experts: Measured 2026-11-02 (docs/STATUS.md): the GPU waits only 1.4% of a prompt pass on expert copies, so the 'CPU experts' experiment cannot win and was closed. Kernel profile (SHADOW_KTIME=1): GPU kernel time per token 9.51 ms = matvec_cols_bf16 1.74 (18%), delta_steps128 1.61 (17%), hc_down_inject_cols_fast_bf16 1.30 (14%), matvec_cols_q5_k 0.60, matvec_cols_f32 0.56, attention ~0.76 (8%), matvec_cols_q4_k 0.47, others. Dense kernels with no tensor-core version (bf16, f32, q5_k, q4_k, hc_down_inject) ~49%.
rules_from_the_user: Measure. What loses stays opt-in (off by default). A change under ~1% is a tie and a tie is a loss (noise floor 0.8% median / 2.0% p90).
Every experiment gets a dated STATUS.md entry (append-only, '## 2026-11-0X: ...') with measured numbers, wins and losses alike.

Do NOT change the decode path (52 tok/s, already beats Strata 47.7), the pinned RAM tier size (36 GiB), or the RAM floor (3 GiB with the 36 GiB tier; 4 GiB default). The machine froze hard at 0.4 GiB free.

Every model load runs under tools/run_capped.ps1. Never push destructive changes. Do not kill processes the user started (a Strata server was running once and the user said 'Stop Strata now' explicitly, so only then).

4. After each kernel: rebuild, correctness gate, interleaved bench, dated STATUS.md entry, commit only the files you changed, push to origin main.
5. Add a unit test or fixture check if the repo has one for mma kernels (grep tests/ for mma_cols) - the existing mma_cols_* kernels are validated somewhere; mirror it for bf16.
how_the_dispatch_works: session.rs fn mv_cols(name, x, xs, y, ys, m): chooses `matvec_cols_<type>` (groups of <=8 tokens, 256 threads) or, with self.tensor_prompt && m >= 16 && type in {Q6_K, IQ4_XS, (BF16 if SHADOW_MMA_BF16=1)} && dims[0] % 64 == 0, launches `mma_cols_<type>` with grid ((rows+63)/64, (m+31)/32), block 128. mma_core<Q> in kernels/matvec.cu stages 64 weight rows x 64 k decoded to half in shared memory (Dec8<Q>::dec8 gives 8 floats) and 32 tokens x 64 k of x converted to half, runs mma.sync m16n8k16 f16 with f32 accumulate. Adding a type = add Dec8<T> + `extern "C" mma_cols_<t>` wrapper + register `cols("mma_cols_<t>")` in kernels.rs (list near line 209) + allow the type in the mv_cols condition. Other callers of the dense matmuls use matvec_cols_multi (line ~3600, router/shared gates; keep exact) and the fused hc_down_inject kernel.
known_findings_to_keep_in_mind: Prompt batch size: a long prompt reads up to 2,048 tokens per pass when the lent cache has room (fixed 2026-11-02: big_batch_on fits rows to the room; ctx 32,768 default gives 768 rows). rows < 512 turns the big batch off.
Fast modes (--tail-skip 3, --tensor-prompt, ...) make near-tie answers differ from --exact; that is normal. Use --exact (EXTRA=--exact) for a reference answer.
SHADOW_STAGE_NO_COPY / SHADOW_STAGE_COPY_EVERY make garbage and crash the router (NaN); do not use them for timing.
Flint tier-flag autotuning is a deferred item the user wants a reminder about after the Strata comparison.
